owner().details: Returns the address of the current owner.

pendingOwner().details: Returns the address of the pending owner.

proxiableUUID().details: Implementation of the ERC-1822 {proxiableUUID} function. This returns the storage slot used by the implementation. It is used to validate the implementation's compatibility when performing an upgrade. IMPORTANT: A proxy pointing at a proxiable contract should not be considered proxiable itself, because this risks bricking a proxy that upgrades to it, by delegating to itself until out of gas. Thus it is critical that this function revert if invoked through a proxy. This is guaranteed by the `notDelegated` modifier.

removeAllowedRecipient(address).details: This function should be idempotent. Unlike `addAllowedRecipient`, no zero-address check      is performed; passing the zero address has no meaningful effect (zero address is never a valid recipient).

secondaryMarketBurnAndRemint(bytes,uint3.details: Checks-effects-interactions: all storage writes happen before the external mint call so      a revert in `TOKEN.mint` rolls back the entire transaction with no partial state.      CEI also ensures a reentrant callback sees `isSecondaryMarketBurned == true` and reverts.

params.balance: The blocklisted balance to burn and re-mint; caller is responsible for off-chain verification
params.domain: The domain on which the burned address resides
params.remintRecipient: The allowlisted recipient to re-mint the balance to
params.secondaryMarketBurnedAddress: The address whose balance is being burned

returns._0: The blocklisted balance, or zero if not SecondaryMarketBurned
The blocklisted balance, or zero if not SecondaryMarketBurned

params.domain: The domain on which the burned address resides
params.txHash: The remint transaction hash to record

returns._0: The SecondaryMarketBurned amount on the domain

transferOwnership(address).details: Starts the ownership transfer of the contract to a new account. Replaces the pending transfer if there is one. Can only be called by the current owner. Setting `newOwner` to the zero address is allowed; this can be used to cancel an initiated ownership transfer.
